args.goal: Design a crewed rocket from the live part catalog, launch it to a stable Kerbin orbit above the atmosphere, then bring the crew home safely

result.goal: Design a crewed rocket from the live part catalog, launch it to a stable Kerbin orbit above the atmosphere, then bring the crew home safely
relevant_lessons: - [2026-06-27] (design) The flown vehicle must be exactly the analysed one: a launch path that re-derived its own design flew a craft with no seat, no legs, and only low-orbit Δv. Copied third-party craft with staging nobody understood over-staged on ascent and under-staged at the transfer burn.

- [2026-06-27] (crew, launch) Crewed pods launched through the old editor/bridge path arrived EMPTY, and an empty crewed pod as the only command part blocked the launch with a "no crew or probe core" dialog. Seat the crew at launch (kRPC launch_vessel crew list) and carry a probe core anyway.

- [2026-06-27] (reentry, process) A rushed live recovery killed five kerbals who were alive in orbit. Test a new reentry on an uncrewed identical capsule first: a stranded crew is recoverable, a botched reentry is not.

- [2026-06-27] (interplanetary, budget) A real crewed Kerbin-to-Duna transfer cost ~3,100 m/s (ejection ~1,039 + corrections ~890 + capture and circularization ~1,176) against ~1,688 m/s modelled, with MechJeb execution overhead ~25%. No fixed transfer-stage margin both launched and captured; precise ejection and cheap capture mattered more than bigger tanks.

- [2026-06-27] (ascent, design) Moving a crew cabin above the capsule decoupler raised the centre of mass and the ascent stalled at ~39 km; a 574 t, 65 m, fineness-17 "needle" was unlaunchable. Radial boosters shorten the core and raise liftoff thrust.

- [2026-06-27] (mechjeb, landing, reentry) MechJeb's landing autopilot owns deorbit, attitude, braking, and chute timing and beat every hand-rolled descent, but from a stable orbit above the atmosphere (a 62 km Duna circle) it never deorbited, and a held SAS retrograde fights it. Put the periapsis into the lower atmosphere yourself, release SAS, then engage.

- [2026-06-27] (krpc) kRPC returns a new proxy object on every .part/.parent/.children access, so Python `is` and id() never match across calls. Compare with == (server object id). An id()-based part-tree walk crossed a decoupler and fired the payload separator on six crewed launches.

- [2026-06-27] (vessel-id) Debris inherits the parent vessel's name: a command addressed by name hit a staged-off booster. Identify vessels by crew, parts (pod, heat shield), orbit, and situation, not by name alone.

args.text: Booster design ASTRA Orbiter 1: Reliant core (2x FL-T800) + 2 Hammer SRBs, Terrier upper stage (FL-T800), Mk1 pod + HeatShield1 + Mk16 chute, RC-001S probe core as backup control. design_check: 23.9 t, liftoff TWR 2.56, stage dv ASL/vac 715/826, 1385/1620, Terrier 3336 vac; ~5.5 km/s vs ~4.0 km/s budget (ascent band 3282-3598 + deorbit + 10%). args.text: Loss of control at 7.3 km: pitch program commanded 55 deg, vehicle held 84-88 deg for the whole climb (autopilot error >25 deg for 4 s at q 20-34 kPa). Cause: no thrust vectoring on the booster (LV-T30 Reliant and RT-10 Hammers do not gimbal) and only ~1.5 kN*m of reaction-wheel torque for a 24 t, 16 m stack; passive fins add stability that resists the turn. Decision: restore pre_launch_orbiter1 and redesign the core with the gimbaled LV-T45 Swivel.

A launch stage whose engines do not gimbal (LV-T30 Reliant, SRBs) cannot follow a gravity-turn program: ASTRA Orbiter 1 (24 t, 16 m, pod+probe wheels ~1.5 kN*m) held 84-88 deg while commanded to 55 deg at 7 km. Check thrust-vectoring authority of the launch stage in design_check before flying.

args.text: EC exhausted (0/65): reaction wheels drained holding attitude through a 23 min coast; no batteries or generation on the design (Terrier has no alternator). Control is full via Jebediah, so steer with the Terrier gimbal while burning: approach periapsis 30 km at <=0.3 throttle, attitude retrograde, guard apoapsis > 90 km. Design lesson for next time: batteries + solar or an alternator engine.

args.text: A crew capsule upper stage with only pod+probe ElectricCharge (65 EC) and no generation lost all power holding attitude through a 23 min coast after circularizing; the deorbit burn was then steered by the Terrier gimbal alone (control stays 'full' with a pilot aboard), and the unpowered Mk1+HeatShield1 capsule entered heat-shield-first on aerodynamic stability. Give coasting stages batteries plus solar/alternator, and release the autopilot on long coasts.

Give coasting stages batteries plus solar/alternator, and release the autopilot on long coasts.

args.text: Staging a Mk16 chute at ~4.4 km and 250 m/s: it semi-deploys at once and only fully opens at its 1,000 m deploy altitude, then slows a 0.94 t Mk1 capsule from ~162 m/s to ~6 m/s within ~650 m (splashdown 3.9 m/s). Arm chutes well above the deploy altitude; a fast fall above ~1 km under a semi-deployed chute is normal.

args.summary: AI-designed ASTRA Orbiter 2 reached an 80.3 x 79.6 km orbit (e=0.0005) and returned Jebediah (splashdown 3.9 m/s). Two anomalies handled in flight: Orbiter 1 could not steer (no gimbal on the booster) and was reverted to checkpoint and redesigned with a Swivel; Orbiter 2 ran out of ElectricCharge in orbit and deorbited on gimbal steering alone. Design checks for steering authority and power were added afterwards.
